scope: Proposition 9.7 (The Boolean extension configuration) of the manuscript “A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem” (preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a102efd4a3009423), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 78. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: If either orientation of the decorated lattice has a finite-group interval representation, there are finite groups A ≤ D, finite nonabelian simple groups T, R, a homomorphism α : A → Aut(T), and extensions βJ : UJ → Aut(T) (∅ ̸= J ⊊ {1, . . . , 4}) with the following properties. Set U∅ = A and β∅ = α. (E1) For nonempty proper J, [A, UJ ] is fenced. If CJ = coreUJ (A), the group UJ /CJ has unique minimal normal subgroup NJ /CJ ∼ = RIJ , UJ = ANJ . (E2) If J ⊊ K ⊊ {1, . . . , 4}, then UJ < UK and βK|UJ = βJ . For nonempty J, the equal-type transport of Proposition 2.6 applies: in particular UJ ∩ NK CK ∼ = NJ CJ , NJ = (UJ ∩ NK)CJ , and the canonical surjections IK → IJ are UJ -equivariant and compose. Whenever a nonempty family of proper subsets has proper union K, its domains generate UK. (E3) All images βJ (UJ ) equal H = α(A) ≥ Inn(T). (E4) If a family of proper nonempty subsets has union {1, . . . , 4}, its homomorphisms have no common extension to the subgroup of D generated by their domains.
